gap: Deferral/exit thresholds in device-edge-cloud cascades are set heuristically (fixed confidence, entropy, DRL reward) with no finite-sample guarantee on end-to-end decision quality.
what_they_do: Choose exit points/offload split to trade accuracy against latency or energy; thresholds tuned empirically on a validation set or learned by a controller optimising an average-case objective.
our_delta: CoDeC certifies P(end-to-end selective risk <= alpha) >= 1-delta over a MULTI-DIMENSIONAL threshold vector using a cost-ordered fixed-sequence Learn-then-Test procedure, and returns the minimum-cost configuration among certified ones.

gap: Conformal/statistically-guaranteed early exit exists only for a single model on a single device, calibrated offline on an i.i.d. labelled set with a scalar threshold.
what_they_do: CATs/CALM calibrate one early-exit threshold so the accelerated model is consistent with the full model with high probability; CRC/LTT give the underlying distribution-free machinery for monotone scalar risk.
our_delta: Extends to a distributed multi-tier pipeline with heterogeneous per-tier cost (compute energy, uplink bytes, cloud monetary, latency); risk is non-monotone in the joint threshold vector, which the cost-ordered test sequence handles while preserving validity.

gap: In deployment a tiered system has no labels EXCEPT the cloud tier's answers on exactly the samples the controller chose to escalate. Recalibrating on that set is biased by the policy itself, silently voiding exchangeability. Not addressed in the edge-cloud literature.
what_they_do: Weighted conformal prediction corrects for covariate shift with known/estimated likelihood ratios; IPW and counterfactual risk minimisation correct logged-bandit selection bias in policy learning, not in calibration of a serving cascade.
our_delta: epsilon-exploration deferral makes the escalation propensity pi(x) KNOWN by construction; propensity-weighted conformal recalibration then restores validity over the full input distribution using only cloud-generated labels. This is the core contribution.

gap: Drift adaptation in cascades is empirical (drift detectors plus retraining); no long-run risk guarantee, and no coupling between risk adaptation and a hard uplink/energy budget.
what_they_do: ACI / conformal PID track coverage online under arbitrary shift for a single predictor; drift surveys cover detection and retraining but target accuracy, not certified risk under a resource budget.
our_delta: Couples online risk tracking to a Lagrangian dual on the uplink budget, giving long-run risk convergence AND budget feasibility in the tiered setting; evaluated on real 36-month sensor drift rather than synthetic shift.

gap: Edge-cloud inference work assumes the cloud is reachable when needed; behaviour and accountability under intermittent connectivity are unspecified.
what_they_do: Model offloading under bandwidth/latency constraints; outages treated as a scheduling or reliability problem, not as a violation of a statistical guarantee.
our_delta: Outage-aware risk-debt accounting: when escalation is impossible the controller switches to abstention/queueing and the unattainable risk is explicitly accounted and repaid, so the guarantee degrades measurably instead of silently.

gap: The cloud tier is treated as ground truth; its own error is never propagated into the reported guarantee.
what_they_do: Learning-to-defer assumes a (near-)oracle expert whose label is correct when consulted; selective classification assumes access to true labels for calibration.
our_delta: Risk is defined both against ground truth and as reference-fidelity to the cloud tier, with a sensitivity analysis quantifying how cloud error inflates certified risk.
